reason_for_new_version: All four full-torus v1 attempts were inconclusive because their interval enclosures remained too loose. Affine-input/remainder propagation improves local bounds, but full two-dimensional coverage may still be expensive. This experiment has a deliberately narrower domain and does not replace or relabel v1.
source_witnesses: The same four fixed seed-zero global readouts passing the recorded feasibility screen: gamma 0.03125, 0.5, 1.0, 8.0. No new fit, checkpoint selection, training, or OOD outcome is used.
domains: Sixteen specified smooth circles: four eligible gamma values times the four class-sector midpoint task coordinates theta = 2*pi*n/8 for n in {1,3,5,7}; phi spans the entire closed periodic interval [0,2*pi].
scope: A certificate applies only to its specified theta circle. Sixteen successful circles would not imply injectivity for every theta, full-torus injectivity, or robust prediction.
arithmetic: python-flint 0.9.0 Arb balls at 128 bits; stored network, embedding and readout coefficients are exact dyadics; theta midpoints are exact rational multiples of mathematical pi.
bounds: Preserve the four ambient input coordinates as affine symbols and propagate interval remainders with the standard centered ReLU relaxation. Use conservative derivative masks and the same residual criterion epsilon < 2/pi. This is an adaptation of established abstract interpretation, not a claimed new abstract domain.
cover: Binary depth-first subdivision of phi. A prefix-free complete binary cover with exact Kraft sum one is mandatory; every leaf is recomputed in standalone replay.
failure_policy: Any unresolved interval, exhausted budget, rejected fixed witness, source mismatch or failed replay prevents certification. All sixteen attempts are retained regardless of outcome.
trust_boundary: Mathematical perturbation argument, source/domain encoding and implementation, Python, and FLINT/Arb. This is not a Lean network-to-graph proof or an independently implemented verifier.
